plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of tiny, fragrant violet-blue flowers. Together they ripple across hillsides in waves of purple and hum with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August, peaking in early to mid July
plants.location: Provence, France, and the wider Mediterranean and temperate Europe
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Dinner-plate-sized pink blossoms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. They open at dawn on still summer ponds and close again by afternoon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early July to August in temperate East Asia
plants.location: Ponds and moats in Japan, China and across temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves shed water and dirt in a way scientists call the 'lotus effect', which has inspired self-cleaning paints and fabrics.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like flowers have drooping rose-purple petals around a spiky, copper-orange central cone. They are a favorite stop for butterflies and goldfinches in sunny meadows and borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: June through September, in full swing in early July
plants.location: Prairies and gardens of the eastern and central United States
plants.funFact: The genus name comes from the Greek 'echinos', meaning hedgehog, a nod to the prickly central cone. Many Native American peoples used the plant medicinally.
